title: Retail Installment Contracts: State Late-Charge Rate Schedule
content:
The late-charge rate of a contract under Retail Installment Contracts follows the company's state late-charge schedule, which turns on two facts on the contract: its contract state and its contract date.

| Contract state | Contract signed | Late-charge rate |
|---|---|---|
| GA, AL, MS or TN | on or after 1 July 2023 | 4.0 percent |
| NC, VA or KY | on or after 1 January 2024 | 3.0 percent |
| any state, any date not covered above | — | the product's late-charge percent |

**Clause.** A contract whose contract state is GA, AL, MS or TN and whose contract date is on or after 2023-07-01 is charged a late-charge rate of 4.0 percent; a contract whose contract state is NC, VA or KY and whose contract date is on or after 2024-01-01 is charged 3.0 percent; every other contract is charged the product's late-charge percent.

The contract state is the borrower's state at signing, whose law governs the contract; the contract date is the date the borrower signed the contract.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical contracts)

| Contract | Rate |
|---|---|
| Georgia, signed 30 June 2023 | the product's late-charge percent (signed before 1 July 2023) |
| Georgia, signed 1 July 2023 | 4.0 percent (on the schedule date) |
| Kentucky, signed 31 December 2023 | the product's late-charge percent |
| Kentucky, signed 1 January 2024 | 3.0 percent |
| Ohio, any date | the product's late-charge percent |

**Basis Q&A.** *Does a borrower who moved to Tennessee after signing a Georgia contract change the rate?* No; the schedule reads the contract state at signing.
